description.p: Spectral runs a chosen microphone through the RNNoise neural network and exposes the result as a native PipeWire virtual microphone that any application can use.

ul.li: Real-time RNNoise denoising with an adjustable voice-activity gate
Native PipeWire virtual source, set as the default input automatically
Built-in voice test to compare original and filtered audio

screenshot.caption: The main window with the virtual microphone active and an input device selected

description.p: Spectral now draws its interface in its own font, Iosevka Aile, so it looks the same on every system, and it has a new icon. The command line suggests what you meant when a command or flag is mistyped, and the Nix package adds a manual page and completions for fish, zsh and bash that include your input device ids. While the microphone is on, the daemon no longer wakes a hundred times a second, and the audio thread no longer takes page faults just after enabling. Closing the terminal that started the window, or pressing Ctrl-C in it, no longer takes the virtual microphone down; an error resolved from the command line now leaves the window; a grayed-out button ignores the keyboard; and an interrupted shutdown no longer leaves the daemon half running.

The virtual microphone now survives its input device being unplugged: it stays available, waits up to thirty seconds for the device to return, and picks it up again by itself — the status reads Reconnecting while it waits. Plugging a device back in no longer confuses the app with a stale id, and unplugging it can no longer silently swap your microphone for the system default. Voice-test recordings are now private to your user account, stop with a clear error when the disk fills, and can no longer be corrupted by a transient write failure. Settings survive two clients applying at once, the window feels quicker to reflect the daemon, and errors open into a details view with a copyable diagnostics summary for bug reports.

The control panel has been redesigned around a resizable layout: an app bar carrying the status, a full-width threshold band, two columns of cards that stretch with the window, and a footer that names every setting still waiting on Apply. The window now fits 768p displays, small text is legible again, and the buttons, switches and slider are drawn in the app's own accent. Applying with nothing changed no longer restarts the live virtual microphone, a voice test stops at the advertised 15 seconds, and every control now reports a name and role to assistive technology.

The interface now uses whichever monospaced font you have configured instead of the one it used to bundle; on every install method except Nix it had been falling back to a proportional face. Audio interfaces whose inputs are split into separate sources are labeled individually rather than appearing as several identical rows. Spectral is also packaged as a Flatpak now, and the virtual microphone works inside the sandbox.

A reliability release for the daemon. Requests no longer hang forever when PipeWire or the daemon stops answering, two daemons started at the same moment can no longer race each other into a broken state, and a voice-test recording abandoned by its client is stopped instead of writing until the disk fills. Refreshing the device list now keeps your selection on the same device.

The virtual-mic name row is a real layout now: Rename and Reset sit beside the name field instead of overlapping it, and the invalid-name flash border is fully visible. Names are capped at 20 characters so a full-length name always fits the field.

Voice-test recording and playback now run as native PipeWire streams inside the daemon rather than spawned pw-record and pw-play processes. This drops the PipeWire tools install dependency and ends orphaned recordings and silent link failures; the saved WAVs and the interface are unchanged.
